The proposed method involves the use of pre-existing deep learning models, which are retrained to adapt to iris recognition tasks. The paper discusses the process of image segmentation, feature extraction, and classification in detail. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional iris recognition techniques in terms of both speed and accuracy. The study also highlights the potential of deep learning in enhancing the performance of biometric systems.

This paper presents a novel approach for iris recognition employing image segmentation through retrained off-the-shelf deep neural networks. The study identifies the limitations of current iris recognition technologies, particularly focusing on instances where non-ideal data has led to incorrect identification. To overcome these challenges, a novel algorithm is introduced, harnessing the power of deep learning that provides superior accuracy when compared to traditional methods. This comprehensive study covers the theoretical explanation of the employed method, followed by a detailed examination of the experimental results. Multiple test scenarios were executed to explore the effectiveness and robustness of the algorithm under adverse conditions including occlusions and contrast variations. Findings indicate a significant improvement in the area of iris recognition, leading to potential implications for advanced bio-metric security applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation of 3D Magnetic Resonance (MR) images, termed as Holistic Decomposition Convolution (HDC). The HDC method aims to address the challenges of complex spatial dependencies and intricate structures in 3D MR images. The proposed method decomposes the 3D convolution into three consecutive 1D convolutions, reducing computational complexity while maintaining the ability to capture 3D contextual information. HDC also incorporates a holistic feature fusion strategy to effectively integrate multi-level features. Extensive experiments on several public datasets demonstrate that HDC outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. The results suggest that HDC could be a promising tool for semantic segmentation in 3D medical image analysis.

This academic paper introduces the Holistic Decomposition Convolution (HDC), a novel technique for enhanced semantic segmentation of three-dimensional Magnetic Resonance (MR) images. Used as a processing tool for the automation of the interpretation of medical data, HDC decouples 3D convolution into multiple directional 2D convolutions to effectively suppress the information loss in segmentation caused by traditional methods, specifically in spatial depth perception. This paper discusses the HDC's potential to provide improved vision in medical imaging applications, particularly in real-time 3D image segmentation tasks. Through extensive experimentation using publicly available brain tumor segmentation benchmarks, the performance of HDC was evaluated, demonstrating promising improvements on segmentation accuracy, efficiency, and generalizability compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

This paper introduces SwipeCut, an interactive image segmentation tool that utilizes diversified seed proposals to enhance user interaction and segmentation accuracy. SwipeCut employs a novel algorithm that generates a diverse set of seed proposals from user-drawn strokes, which are then used to produce multiple segmentation results. The user can interactively select the most accurate segmentation from these results, reducing the need for repetitive fine-tuning. Experimental results demonstrate that SwipeCut outperforms existing interactive segmentation methods in terms of both efficiency and accuracy. The tool's user-friendly interface and high performance make it a promising solution for various applications, including object extraction, image editing, and computer vision tasks.

This research paper presents SwipeCut, an innovative tool designed to improve interactive object segmentation in digital images. SwipeCut utilizes a unique method of diversified seed proposals, which extends the traditional graph-cut algorithm, creating a highly efficient, user-friendly interactive segmentation system. We evaluate the proposed method on a variety of image types and segmentation tasks, demonstrating its superior performance compared to existing tools. Functioning with minimal user interactions, SwipeCut can successfully extract complex objects from their backgrounds, proving its unparalleled significance in the field of image processing and computer vision.

This paper presents a novel approach to fast matrix-vector products for the graph Laplacian of fully connected networks by combining Non-equispaced Fast Fourier Transform (NFFT) and Krylov methods. The proposed method significantly reduces the computational complexity and memory requirements, making it feasible for large-scale networks. The paper provides a detailed analysis of the algorithm, demonstrating its efficiency and accuracy through various numerical experiments. The results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods in terms of speed and scalability, opening new avenues for the analysis and design of fully connected networks.

This paper explores the combination of non-equispaced fast Fourier transform (NFFT) and Krylov methods, to facilitate expeditious matrix-vector products for the graph Laplacian in fully connected networks. The study pioneers an approach utilising these methods to reduce the computational complexity of existing algorithms. Specifically, it presents the NFFT-based fast matrix-vector multiplication method which effectively supports the calculation of graph Laplacian of fully connected networks. Furthermore, the incorporation of Krylov techniques is examined to achieve rapid solvability of large-scale systems. The research underscores significant improvements in performance due to the synergistic effect of NFFT and Krylov methods, thereby offering a potential solution to overcome the computational constraints in evaluating matrix-vector products for complex and dense graphs. The paper also includes a series of experiments validating the improvements in computation speed and efficiency, prompting further exploration in real-world applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to the segmentation of IsoIntense Infant Brain MRI using Deep 3D Fully Convolutional DenseNets. The proposed method employs exclusive independent probability estimation to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process. The DenseNets architecture is utilized to extract and fuse high-level features from different scales, which significantly improves the discriminative capability of the model. The exclusive independent probability estimation further refines the segmentation results by considering the exclusive relationship among different classes. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This study provides a promising tool for the automatic and accurate segmentation of IsoIntense Infant Brain MRI, which is crucial for the early diagnosis and treatment of various neurological disorders.

In this paper, we propose and implement an innovative approach towards independent probability estimation by utilizing Deep 3D Fully Convolutional DenseNets (FCDenseNets) and uniquely applying it to the significant task of IsoIntense Infant Brain MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) Segmentation. The complexity of this segmentation arises from the high similarity in intensity values of different tissue types, leading to indistinguishable boundaries in infant brain MRIs. Our method demonstrates robust performance in isolating these boundaries and precisely segmenting the brain algorithms demonstrating a significant improvement over conventional methods. Experimental results validate the efficacy of our approach, with promising potential for generalization to other intensity indistinguishable segmentation tasks in biomedical imaging. This paper further elucidates the detailed implementation, experimentation, outcomes, and potential future applications of our proposed method.

This paper presents a novel approach for brain tumor segmentation and overall survival prediction using an ensemble of 3D U-Nets and radiomic features. The study focuses on the application of deep learning techniques for the accurate segmentation of brain tumors from MRI scans. The proposed method utilizes an ensemble of 3D U-Nets, which significantly improves the segmentation performance by leveraging the strengths of multiple models. Furthermore, the paper explores the use of radiomic features for predicting the overall survival of patients. These features, extracted from the segmented tumor regions, provide valuable insights into tumor characteristics that are strongly correlated with patient survival. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both segmentation accuracy and survival prediction. This research contributes to the advancement of medical imaging analysis and has potential implications for personalized treatment planning in neuro-oncology.

This paper presents an innovative approach to brain tumor segmentation and overall survival prediction utilizing an ensemble of 3D U-Nets and radiomic features. The study employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to improve brain tumor segmentation accuracy, particularly the U-Net model, known for its efficiency in biomedical image segmentation. Tests involving the 3D U-Net ensemble show usability in differentiating healthy tissue from tumors in brain biopsy images. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates the application of radiomic features to predict an individual's overall survival rate after tumor detection. Based on quantitative imaging characteristics, these radiomic features enable objective and repeatable measurements. This research aims to contribute to the body of knowledge in the medical field, essentially in brain tumor diagnosis and prognosis, enhancing patient care strategies in the future.

This paper presents a novel approach to joint segmentation and localization in videos and images through foreground clustering. The study introduces a new algorithm that effectively distinguishes foreground objects from the background, enabling more accurate object localization. The proposed method is based on a combination of spatial-temporal information and color-texture features, which allows for robust segmentation and localization even in complex visual scenes. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The results suggest that foreground clustering can be a powerful tool for various applications in computer vision, including object tracking, scene understanding, and video surveillance.

This paper addresses the task of joint segmentation and localization in both videos and images by introducing a novel method, 'Foreground Clustering'. The method oversees identifying and clustering foreground pixels that share similar object-level properties while discerning them from the background. The authors articulate a new algorithm that assimilates both spatial and temporal cues, simultaneously localizing and segmenting foreground objects efficiently. It surpasses traditional methods, which perform these tasks separately, improving both accuracy and speed. The presented experimental results show that this Foreground Clustering method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques on several benchmark datasets, leading to more precise and efficient segmentation and localization in videos and images.

This paper presents RA-UNet, a novel hybrid deep attention-aware network designed to extract liver and tumor regions from CT scans. The proposed model combines the strengths of the U-Net architecture and a residual attention mechanism to enhance feature representation and focus on target regions. The RA-UNet model was trained and tested on a publicly available dataset, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and Dice coefficient compared to other state-of-the-art models. The results suggest that the RA-UNet model can effectively assist in the automatic and accurate extraction of liver and tumor regions, potentially improving the efficiency and accuracy of cancer diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents the RA-UNet, a hybrid deep attention-aware network designed for efficient extraction of liver and tumor regions from Computed Tomography (CT) scans. The proposed network integrates attention-gated, residual, and UNet-like architectures for improved performance on tasks such as feature extraction and image segmentation. It is hypothesized that the network can consistently identify and delineate liver and tumor regions in CT scans, even in cases with varying degrees of clarity or ambiguity. Experimental results, based on the LiTS 2017 and 3DIRCAD public databases, demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms other state-of-the-art methods for liver and tumor segmentation in CT images. The RA-UNet is a promising tool in medical imaging, cancer diagnosis, and treatment planning, due to its automatic, efficient, and accurate extraction capabilities.

This paper presents a novel approach to the dense deformable registration of volume images using fast graph-cut based optimization. The proposed method addresses the computational challenges associated with traditional methods, offering a more efficient and practical solution for image registration. The algorithm leverages the power of graph-cut optimization to quickly and accurately align images, even in the presence of significant deformations. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of our method in terms of speed and accuracy compared to existing techniques. This work has significant implications for various applications, including medical imaging, computer vision, and machine learning, where accurate and efficient image registration is crucial.

This academic paper features a novel, practical, and efficient optimization method for dense deformable registration of volume images. Our approach hinges mainly on the Graph-Cut algorithm, a globally optimal and computationally efficient method that directly solves the registration problem in a dense volumetric manner. Specifically optimized for practical applications, we also introduce a multi-scale and multi-level optimization strategy aimed at improving computational efficiency and registration accuracy. The outcomes from our proposed technique are validated on various volume data including brain MRI volumes, abdominal CT volumes, and synthetic volumes from datasets. Results show that our Graph-Cut-Based method delivers significantly improved registration accuracy and execution speed than the state-of-the-art techniques, suggesting its potential uses for fields that require intensive volume image features, such as medical diagnosis and scientific visualization.

This paper presents a novel domain adaptation framework for medical image segmentation, addressing the challenge of applying machine learning models to new domains with different distributions. The proposed framework leverages unsupervised learning techniques to adapt a pre-trained model to a target domain, reducing the need for extensive annotated data. It also incorporates a unique loss function to enhance the segmentation performance. Experimental results on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in improving the accuracy and robustness of medical image segmentation. This work contributes to the advancement of machine learning applications in healthcare, particularly in medical imaging analysis, and opens up new avenues for further research in domain adaptation techniques.

This paper presents a novel domain adaptation framework designed for medical image segmentation. The need for this framework arises due to the existing shortcomings in handling domain shift brought about by image acquisition variations. The proposed model effectively addresses this issue by leveraging a two-level neural architecture. The first level is dedicated to defining and learning domain-invariant features, while the second level is tasked with task-specific fine-tuning for segmentation. Experiments involving MRI and CT scan images show promising results, highlighting the success of this model in achieving robust segmentation performance despite domain shift. This method offers a new way forward for enhancing the effectiveness and efficiency of medical image analysis, particularly in scenarios where acquiring vast amounts of annotated data is challenging.

This paper presents a novel approach to interactive image segmentation using a fully convolutional two-stream fusion network. The proposed method leverages both local and global context information to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation. The two-stream network consists of a local stream that captures fine details and a global stream that understands the overall layout. These two streams are then fused to generate the final segmentation result. The proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The paper also includes extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

This paper introduces a Fully Convolutional Two-Stream Fusion Network (FCTSFN) for interactive image segmentation tasks. The FCTSFN employs a two-stream structure to handle various features in input images and to capture spatial details and high-level semantic information. The primary stream is designed for processing the foreground and background features separately, while the secondary stream is constructed for learning the residual object between the predicted and ground truth labels using convolutional operations. Consequently, the two-stream network integrates interactive information into a unified framework, extracting the precise boundaries of objects and improving the overall segmentation accuracy significantly. Experimental results illustrate that the FCTSFN delivers superior performances compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of precision, recall, and intersection-over-union metrics. This novel framework provides an effective solution for complex interactive image segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel gradient-based algorithm for effective cloud detection and segmentation in satellite imagery. The proposed method aims to enhance the accuracy of the Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information using Artificial Neural Networks-Cloud Classification System (PERSIANN-CCS). The algorithm employs a gradient-based approach to detect and segment clouds, overcoming the limitations of traditional threshold-based methods. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using various satellite datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in cloud detection accuracy and segmentation quality. The enhanced PERSIANN-CCS, incorporating the proposed algorithm, shows promising results in precipitation estimation, potentially contributing to more accurate weather forecasting and climate studies.

This paper presents an innovative approach to cloud detection and segmentation using a gradient-based algorithm in the field of satellite imagery. The focus of the study is the establishment of an improved PERSIANN-CCS system. Through comprehensive testing and validation, it was found that the proposed method is capable of effectively detecting and delineating cloud structures against clear-sky backgrounds. The implemented system displayed better performance compared to other traditional methods in terms of accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness when confronted with different atmospheric and illumination conditions. This study proposes a novel and feasible solution to the challenges faced in cloud detection and segmentation, contributing significantly to weather forecasting and climate monitoring applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to 3D segmentation, specifically designed to handle datasets with highly unbalanced object sizes. The proposed method employs an exponential logarithmic loss function, which effectively addresses the challenges posed by the significant size disparity among objects. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the proposed method, demonstrating its superior performance over traditional loss functions in handling unbalanced data. The results show that the method significantly improves the accuracy of 3D segmentation tasks, making it a promising tool for applications in various fields such as medical imaging, robotics, and computer vision.

This paper introduces a new method for 3D segmentation of datasets containing objects of highly unbalanced sizes, utilizing an exponential logarithmic loss function. Traditional methods often struggle with these datasets, inaccurately segmenting smaller objects due to the large object size imbalances. The novel exponential logarithmic loss function mitigates this issue by weighting object pixel contributions based on size, ensuring accurate segmentation across differing scales. The proposed method was tested on a variety of datasets and demonstrated superior results compared to existing techniques, indicating its potential value in applications such as biomedical imaging, where object size discrepancy is commonly encountered. Further research is suggested to explore its potential in broader settings and its integration with modern deep learning-based segmentation methods.

This paper presents a novel time series graph cut image segmentation scheme specifically designed for liver tumors. The proposed method leverages the temporal information in time series medical images to improve the accuracy and robustness of tumor segmentation. The scheme integrates the graph cut algorithm with a time series analysis, which effectively captures the temporal changes in tumor growth and enhances the segmentation performance. Experimental results on a dataset of liver CT images demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional image segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. This research has significant implications for improving the diagnosis and treatment planning of liver cancer.

This paper presents a novel method for the segmentation of liver tumors using a time series graph cut image segmentation scheme. This technique combines temporal information captured in different phases of contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) scanned images with spatial information in 3D data sets, thus extending the conventional graph cut algorithm. Our experimental results reveal that the proposed model offers superior robustness and accuracy when compared to conventional segmentation methods, particularly in distinguishing between tumor and non-tumor regions. The paper also discusses the usefulness of the method in clinical settings, and suggests the potential for further applications in other organ-specific tumor detection and segmentation.

This paper introduces YouTube-VOS, a large-scale video object segmentation benchmark that provides a comprehensive analysis of the performance of various state-of-the-art video object segmentation algorithms. The benchmark is based on a new dataset, which is the largest of its kind, containing over 4,000 high-quality, manually annotated video sequences, involving 94 object categories. The paper also presents a new evaluation metric that takes into account both the spatial and temporal aspects of video object segmentation. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the benchmark in evaluating and comparing different algorithms, and highlight the challenges and opportunities in video object segmentation research.

This academic paper introduces "YouTube-VOS", the first large-scale video object segmentation benchmark. With over 4,400 videos of over 94 object categories, YouTube-VOS provides a comprehensive and diverse dataset for video object segmentation. Furthermore, this paper presents a new model, dubbed RGMP (Recurrent Graph-based Network Propagation), designed to address the unique challenges within the video object segmentation field. Extensive experiments reveal that the RGMP model significantly outperforms current segmentation method on several evaluation metrics. YouTube-VOS contributes to advancing the research in video understanding and may potentially lead to significant practical applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to iris recognition using a database of iris images obtained in visible light using a smartphone camera. The study aims to explore the feasibility and effectiveness of using smartphone cameras for iris recognition, a biometric identification method traditionally reliant on infrared imaging. The paper discusses the creation of a unique database of iris images, the challenges encountered due to varying light conditions, and the image processing techniques employed to enhance the quality of images. The proposed recognition algorithm's performance is evaluated and compared with existing methods. The results demonstrate that iris recognition using visible light smartphone images is a promising avenue for biometric identification, with potential applications in mobile security and authentication.

This study presents a novel research approach in iris recognition using a database of iris images obtained in visible light using a smartphone camera. The primary focus lies in identifying the opportunities and limitations of harnessing visible light photography for iris recognition, a markedly different method from traditional near-infrared (NIR) captures. The paper discusses the methodology employed in capturing, processing, and analyzing the images along with a comparative evaluation against conventional NIR techniques. Furthermore, an in-depth investigation is conducted into the current smartphone technologies' potential in serving as feasible platforms for iris recognition in biometric authentication systems. The results exhibit promising potential towards the realization of convenient, cost-efficient, and reliable iris recognition with consumer-grade smartphone devices.

This paper presents a novel approach for the segmentation of microscopy data to identify nuclei in divergent images. The study addresses the challenges of variability in size, density, and texture of nuclei across different types of biological images. The proposed method combines machine learning algorithms with image processing techniques to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of nuclei detection. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in the segmentation performance compared to existing methods, thereby providing a robust tool for biological and medical research. The paper also discusses potential applications of this method in disease diagnosis, drug discovery, and cell biology studies.

This academic paper presents a comprehensive study on the segmentation of microscopy data aimed at identifying nuclei in varied types of imaging modalities. The complexity and diversity of microscopy images necessitates the development of robust, high-precision algorithms for accurate nuclei detection. The paper details a unique, comprehensive image analysis method that adapts to different image conditions, along with various morphological characteristics of the nuclei. It compares the developed method with the existing techniques on several datasets, showing promising accuracy and improved performance in diverse image scenarios. This research has potential implications in fast-paced analysis of microscopy data, improving diagnostic accuracy in pathological laboratories, and furthering our understanding of cellular structures and functions.

This paper introduces Concept Mask, a novel approach to large-scale segmentation based on semantic concepts. The study addresses the challenges of traditional segmentation methods, such as the need for extensive manual annotation and the inability to handle diverse and complex scenes. Concept Mask leverages deep learning techniques and semantic understanding to automatically segment images at a large scale. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The results suggest that Concept Mask can effectively facilitate various computer vision tasks, including object detection, scene understanding, and image editing.

This academic paper introduces a novel technique called "Concept Mask", designed for large-scale segmentation from semantic concepts. Leveraging advanced computational models, the technique improves the accurate interpretation of visual data, enhancing its algorithmic segmentation capabilities. It particularly focuses on interpreting and distinguishing semantic concepts within diverse and complex datasets. Concept Mask's extraordinary scalability aids in processing substantial visual data volumes, making it a pioneering approach within computer vision, image processing, and machine learning domains. This paper explores the fundamental methodology of the Concept Mask, detailing its working mechanism, benefits over conventional methods, application potential, and performance evaluation outcomes. Experimental results show that the Concept Mask outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of efficiency, scalability, and accuracy.

This paper presents a novel 3D Coarse-to-Fine (C2F) framework for volumetric medical image segmentation. The proposed method aims to address the challenges of high computational cost and lack of accuracy in existing segmentation techniques. The C2F framework employs a two-stage process: a coarse segmentation stage that quickly identifies regions of interest, followed by a fine segmentation stage that refines these regions with high precision. The framework is designed to be adaptable to various types of medical imaging modalities and demonstrates superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency when compared to state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results on multiple public medical datasets confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework. This research has significant implications for improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning in healthcare.

This paper presents a novel 3D coarse-to-fine framework for volumetric medical image segmentation, particularly employed for isolating and identifying various anatomical structures in medical volumes. The framework incorporates a two-stage process: an initial segmentation using lower-resolution images and subsequent refinement at a higher resolution. This methodology significantly boosts the efficiency and accuracy of the segmentation process. Various experiments consistently demonstrate the superior performance of our model over traditional single-stage methods, illustrating its potential usability in several medical applications, such as diagnosis support, surgical planning, and treatment monitoring. Future developments are discussed, focusing on prospective integration with deep learning methods.

This paper presents a novel multi-contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) approach for thalamus segmentation. The thalamus, a crucial part of the human brain, has been challenging to segment due to its complex structure and the presence of surrounding tissues with similar intensity profiles. The proposed method leverages the complementary information from different MRI contrasts to improve the segmentation accuracy. The approach was tested on a dataset of healthy subjects and patients with various neurological disorders. The results demonstrate that the multi-contrast MRI approach significantly outperforms single-contrast methods, providing more accurate and robust thalamus segmentation. This advancement could potentially enhance the understanding of the thalamus's role in various neurological disorders and improve the effectiveness of related treatments.

This paper presents a novel approach for thalamus segmentation using multi-contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). The focus of the study is to enhance the accuracy, efficiency, and effectiveness of thalamus identification and volumetric analysis in the human brain via MRI. The method utilized a combination of T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted contrasts to differentiate between thalamus and non-thalamus structures. Experimental results indicate that our multi-contrast MRI approach significantly improves thalamus segmentation compared to traditional single-contrast methods, promising potential applications in studying various neurological conditions that impact the thalamus.

This paper presents UNet++, a novel and more advanced architecture based on the U-Net model, specifically designed for medical image segmentation. The proposed model addresses the issue of semantic segmentation of medical images, which is a critical task in many medical applications. UNet++ introduces a series of nested, dense skip pathways to the original U-Net, aiming to capture and combine low-level image details and high-level semantic features more effectively. The paper provides a comprehensive comparison between UNet++ and the original U-Net, demonstrating that the proposed architecture consistently outperforms the baseline model across various datasets and three different tasks: nuclei segmentation, liver segmentation, and lung segmentation. The results suggest that UNet++ could be a promising tool for medical image analysis.

This academic paper presents UNet++, an enhanced architecture of U-Net for medical image segmentation. Our novel nested and dense architecture addresses two major concerns in the original U-Net: the unnecessarily deep feature maps in the decoder sub-network, and the escalated semantic gap in deep layers. Our extensive comparative study demonstrates that UNet++ achieves superior performance to U-net on various biomedical image segmentation datasets. Besides improved accuracy, UNet++ simplifies the network architecture by reducing the requirement for extensive architectural engineering. This design simplifies the implementation and improves the efficiency in applications, crucial for medical image analysis. Despite its primary adoption in biomedical image analysis, UNet++ could also be generalized for other image segmentation tasks due to its robustness and efficiency.

This paper presents a novel approach to the segmentation of post-mortem iris images using data-driven techniques. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of iris recognition systems in forensic investigations. The proposed method involves the use of machine learning algorithms to analyze and segment iris images, overcoming the challenges posed by post-mortem changes such as corneal clouding and pupil dilation. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in the segmentation accuracy compared to traditional methods, thereby enhancing the reliability of iris-based biometric identification in forensic applications. The paper also discusses potential future developments in this field, including the integration of this technique into automated identification systems.

This academic paper presents an innovative study on data-driven segmentation of post-mortem iris images. The research is predicated on creating effective strategies for enhancing security measures which includes the biometric identification of deceased individuals. Using advanced algorithms and image processing techniques, high-resolution post-mortem iris images were successfully segmented for data analysis purposes. Further, the paper discusses the unique challenges associated with post-mortem iris recognition like pupillary dilatation, corneal clouding, and others. The findings of the study could have significant implications for forensic science and could revolutionize post-mortem individual identification procedures. This study also advances the ongoing discussions about the use and development of biometric technologies for the purpose of individual identification.

This paper investigates the relationship between function norms and regularization in deep networks. It explores the theoretical underpinnings of how function norms can be used as a form of regularization in deep learning models, and how this can potentially improve their generalization performance. The paper also presents empirical results demonstrating the effectiveness of function norm regularization in various deep learning tasks. The findings suggest that function norm regularization can be a valuable tool for improving the robustness and performance of deep networks. The paper concludes with a discussion on the implications of these findings for the design and training of deep learning models.

This paper offers a deep dive into the intricacies of function norms and regularization in deep networks, which are crucial factors in modern machine learning technology. The primary focus lies on exploring and redefining the role of function norms, the implicit bias of optimization, and the process of regularization within the context of deep networks. The study introduces a new perspective on these topics, presenting several experiments and analyses that demonstrate their interconnectedness and impact on achieving optimal solutions. The findings promise to shed new light on the design, training and generalization of deep networks, potentially paving the way towards improving and refining these crucial aspects of machine learning models.

This paper presents a novel method for fully automatic myocardial segmentation of contrast echocardiography sequences using random forests guided by a shape model. The proposed method combines the strengths of machine learning and statistical shape models to achieve accurate and robust segmentation. The random forest classifier is trained to recognize myocardial tissues based on intensity, texture, and temporal features, while the shape model guides the segmentation process to ensure anatomical plausibility. The method was evaluated on a dataset of 100 patients and demonstrated superior performance compared to existing methods in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the field of medical image analysis by providing a reliable tool for automatic myocardial segmentation, which is crucial for the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases.

This academic paper presents a novel method for fully automatic myocardial segmentation of contrast echocardiography sequences using shape models guided by random forests. The study's goal is to improve the identification and analysis of cardiovascular diseases. The proposed method combines the robustness of a statistical shape model with the flexibility of a machine learning based approach. Experimental results obtained from real clinical data demonstrate the efficiency and superior performance of our approach over existing methods, both in terms of accuracy and computational time. Our method is reliable and can be used to facilitate the analysis of large quantities of diagnostic data, improving patient care in cardiology.

This paper presents a novel approach to predicting the quality of segmentation in real-time. The study focuses on developing an algorithm that can accurately assess the quality of segmentation without the need for ground truth data. The proposed method leverages machine learning techniques to predict segmentation quality based on features extracted from the segmented data. The results demonstrate that our approach can effectively predict the quality of segmentation in real-time, thereby enabling immediate corrective actions and improving overall segmentation performance. This work has significant implications for various applications, including image processing, computer vision, and medical imaging, where real-time and accurate segmentation is crucial.

This paper presents a novel approach to the real-time prediction of segmentation quality, a key challenge in the field of computer vision. It explores an innovative algorithm that utilizes both temporal and spatial features to make accurate, real-time assessments of segmentation quality. The algorithm is validated through an extensive experimental analysis, illustrating its superior performance compared to existing methods. This research introduces a highly efficient and reliable tool that could significantly improve the effectiveness and precision of numerous applications requiring image and video segmentation, thus opening new avenues for advancements in areas like autonomous driving, video surveillance, and medical imaging.

This paper presents a novel approach to improving the performance of Fully Convolutional Networks (FCNs) by concurrently applying spatial and channel squeeze and excitation. The proposed method, termed Concurrent Spatial and Channel Squeeze & Excitation (cSSE), aims to recalibrate the feature maps in both spatial and channel dimensions simultaneously. The cSSE module is lightweight and can be easily integrated into existing FCNs without significant computational overhead. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that FCNs equipped with the proposed cSSE module achieve superior performance compared to their counterparts without cSSE. The paper also provides an in-depth analysis of the effects of cSSE on the learning capability and generalization performance of FCNs.

This paper presents a study on the integration of Concurrent Spatial And Channel Squeeze & Excitation (cScaSE) in Fully Convolutional Networks (FCNs) for enhancing performance. The study reveals that incorporating spatial and channel attention simultaneously provides significant improvements in particular tasks such as semantic segmentation. We introduce a new modular architecture designed to capture complementary and diverse features from both channel-wise and spatial dimensions. The proposed method, with three different applications, achieved a substantial margin over baseline on benchmark datasets. This research illuminates a path to boost the efficiency of FCNs, providing deeper insights for future work in this area.

This paper introduces Coarse to Fine Context Memory (CFCM), a novel approach for image segmentation. CFCM leverages the contextual information in an image, processing it from a coarse to fine perspective to enhance the segmentation performance. The proposed method utilizes a memory module to store and retrieve the contextual information, which is then used to guide the segmentation process. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that CFCM outperforms existing state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The paper also provides a comprehensive analysis of the proposed method, highlighting its advantages and potential applications in various image processing tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach for image segmentation - Coarse to Fine Context Memory (CFCM). CFCM addresses the issue of information loss in conventional methods by storing different levels of context information in separate memory modules. The methodology first captures coarse global context, followed by a progressive refinement process to enhance local details, thus successfully incorporating both local and global information for accurate segmentation. Evaluation of CFCM on various benchmark datasets validates its superior performance over other current state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms. It has a wide range of applications in image processing, medical imaging, and autonomous driving, among others.

This paper presents a novel approach to 3D shape segmentation using Shape Fully Convolutional Networks (Shape FCN). The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to segment 3D shapes into meaningful parts. Unlike traditional methods that rely on hand-crafted features, Shape FCN learns features directly from raw 3D shape data in an end-to-end manner. The network architecture is designed to capture both local and global shape information, enabling accurate and robust segmentation. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of Shape FCN over state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. This work opens up new possibilities for 3D shape analysis and understanding.

This paper presents a novel method for 3D shape segmentation using Shape Fully Convolutional Networks (Shape FCNs). The approach leverages the power of 3D deep learning techniques, adopting a voxel-based representation for 3D shapes, and a fully convolutional network architecture, enabling end-to-end learning from 3D data. Unlike previous methods which require complex pre-processing or fail to fully capture 3D shape structures, our method directly processes raw 3D data and captures both local and global shape information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Shape FCNs in a variety of experiments on standard benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance with significant improvements over existing methods. This research lays a foundation for additional work in automated 3D shape segmentation and similar image processing tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach to medical image segmentation, specifically focusing on the pancreas, a challenging and variably located organ. We introduce the Attention U-Net, a deep learning model that incorporates an attention mechanism to guide the model where to focus in an image. The model is trained and evaluated on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans. The results demonstrate that the Attention U-Net outperforms traditional U-Net models, providing more accurate and consistent pancreas segmentation. This research has significant implications for improving the accuracy of automated medical image analysis, potentially leading to better diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper offers a detailed exploration of the Attention U-Net, a variant of the convolutional neural network U-Net, and its value in medical image analysis, specifically in targeting the pancreas. Traditional networks often fall short in such nuanced tasks due to the organ's complex anatomical environment. To address this, the Attention U-Net architecture is introduced, learning to attend to particular target regions with complex backgrounds. This study evaluates the method's performance via quantitative comparisons with standard U-Net on a publicly available dataset. The findings confirm that Attention U-Net surpasses the regular U-Net in identifying the pancreas, marking a significant advancement in the field. The paper also discusses potential applications in other challenging medical imaging tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach to interactive medical image segmentation, combining point-based interaction and sequential patch learning. The proposed method allows users to interactively guide the segmentation process by providing point-based inputs, which are then used to train a patch-based machine learning model. The model is trained sequentially, incorporating user inputs iteratively to improve segmentation accuracy. The proposed method was evaluated on various medical imaging datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. This approach has potential applications in improving the accuracy of medical image analysis and enhancing the efficiency of clinical workflows.

This paper presents a novel approach for interactive medical image segmentation through point-based interaction and sequential patch learning. Many existing methods require extensive manual effort or yet lack accuracy. The proposed method aims to reduce the need for massive manual annotation, increasing the accuracy and fluosity of segmentation. The method integrates a novel interaction strategy, a patch-based learning model, and a dedicated training strategy to tackle this issue. The user inputs points of different classes, and the system generates segmentation results interactively, refining the results through sequential learning. The experimental evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and user experience. Furthermore, it outperforms benchmark methods on multiple medical image datasets, proving to be promising for practical use in medical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel approach to ballast degradation evaluation using a machine vision algorithm implemented in Matlab. Ballast degradation is a critical issue in railway maintenance and its accurate assessment is crucial for ensuring safety and efficiency. Traditional methods of evaluation are often time-consuming and subjective. To address these challenges, we propose a machine vision algorithm that can automatically analyze and quantify the degree of ballast degradation. The algorithm is designed to process and analyze images of ballast, identify the key features associated with degradation, and provide a quantitative measure of the degradation level. The implementation of the algorithm in Matlab allows for efficient processing and easy integration with existing systems. The results from our study demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of our proposed method, suggesting its potential for practical applications in railway maintenance.

In this paper, we present the development and implementation of a Machine Vision Algorithm using MATLAB to evaluate ballast degradation, an important aspect in the maintenance and efficiency of railway track systems. The algorithm employs image processing techniques to monitor and assess the physical and operational conditions of the track ballast. Methods include segmentation, morphological operations, feature extraction and classification. Results have shown that the proposed algorithm enhances the inspection and monitoring process, enabling an early detection of degradations thus reducing the preventive maintenance costs while enhancing safety and reliability. This research illuminates the potential of incorporating machine vision technology and automated systems in railway track maintenance, opening avenues for future research in this area.

This paper presents a novel approach to pathology image segmentation using unsupervised representation learning with spherical K-means. The study aims to overcome the limitations of supervised methods that require extensive labeled data and are often biased towards the training set. Our method leverages the power of unsupervised learning to extract meaningful features from pathology images, which are then clustered using spherical K-means. The proposed approach is evaluated on several pathology image datasets, demonstrating superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods. The results suggest that unsupervised representation learning with spherical K-means offers a promising direction for efficient and effective pathology image segmentation.

This paper proposes an unsupervised method for pathology image segmentation by utilizing representation learning with Spherical K-means. Traditional image segmentation methods suffer from heavy dependency on supervised learning or handcrafted features, leading to human error and imprecision. We solve this by using a combination of transfer learning and Spherical K-means clustering for task-agnostic feature extraction, capturing vital visual features without explicit supervision. The proposed approach is experimentally validated on several public pathology image datasets demonstrating substantial performance enhancement compared to conventional methods. This novel approach to pathology image segmentation could improve the reliability of medical diagnoses and yield new insights in digital pathology.

This paper presents a novel approach to training multi-organ segmentation networks using a method called Sample Selection by Relaxed Upper Confident Bound (SSR-UCB). The study aims to address the challenge of imbalanced data distribution in medical image analysis, which often leads to sub-optimal performance in organ segmentation tasks. The proposed SSR-UCB method selects informative samples for training based on their uncertainties and difficulties, thereby improving the learning efficiency and segmentation performance. Experimental results on two public datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis and has potential applications in clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.

This academic paper introduces a novel methodology for training multi-organ segmentation networks using Sample Selection by Relaxed Upper Confident Bound (R-UCB). The traditional techniques often falter when dealing with large-scale multi-organ segmentation due to inconsistent annotation quality in medical imaging datasets. Our proposed method incorporates an R-UCB based sample selection strategy into the network training process which enables the model to select more informative samples for training. Experimental results demonstrated that our method significantly improved the performance of multi-organ segmentation networks in comparison to existing methods. The research offers an effective solution to the long-standing problem of data inconsistency in large-scale medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation, termed Compassionately Conservative Balanced Cuts (CCBC). The CCBC method aims to strike a balance between the two extremes of overly conservative and overly liberal segmentation, which often result in under-segmentation and over-segmentation respectively. The proposed method introduces a new energy function that incorporates both local and global information, ensuring a more accurate and balanced segmentation. Experimental results on various image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the CCBC method in achieving high-quality segmentation, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The paper also discusses potential applications of the CCBC method in various fields such as computer vision, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper introduces a novel approach to image segmentation, named Compassionately Conservative Balanced Cuts (CCBC). Unlike conventional methods, the CCBC strategy adeptly balances the trade-off between boundary simplicity and region homogeneity while being particularly conscious of preserving and protecting less prominent patterns, an aspect we metaphorically termed "compassionate". A unique mathematical formulation is employed to redefine the task of segmentation, combining graph theory and continuous optimization, and leading to a more efficient and accurate segmentation. Experimental results indicate that this approach outperforms existing methods in capturing intricate details and maintaining image balance, thereby enhancing the reliability and vision clarity of image segmentation. This method promises broad applicability in machine learning, computer vision, and image analysis.

This paper presents an innovative adaptive strategy for superpixel-based region-growing image segmentation. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by dynamically adjusting the growth criteria of superpixels based on local image features. The strategy involves an initial superpixel segmentation followed by an adaptive region-growing process, which refines the segmentation results by merging or splitting superpixels. Experimental results on various image datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional region-growing methods in terms of both segmentation quality and computational efficiency. This research has significant implications for applications requiring precise image segmentation, such as medical imaging, object recognition, and computer vision.

This paper presents a novel adaptive strategy for superpixel-based region-growing image segmentation. The study focuses on enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation, crucial for tasks such as object recognition, scene understanding, and medical imaging. The proposed approach modifies traditional superpixel methods by incorporating an adaptive region-growing algorithm, resulting in a robust and sophisticated framework that can handle complex and noisy images. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed strategy’s superior performance, with improved precision and reduced computational time compared to conventional methods. The findings suggest that the model has high potential for adapting to various segmentation tasks, signifying a significant contribution to image processing technology.

This paper introduces the Inhomogeneity Estimation by Orthogonal Primary Functions (IEOPF), a novel active contour model for image segmentation. The model is designed to handle images with inhomogeneities, a common challenge in image processing. The IEOPF model employs orthogonal primary functions to estimate the inhomogeneity, which is then incorporated into the energy functional of the active contour model. The proposed model is tested on synthetic and real images, demonstrating its effectiveness in segmenting images with inhomogeneities. The results show that the IEOPF model outperforms existing models in terms of accuracy and robustness. This research contributes to the field of image processing by providing a new approach to handle inhomogeneities in image segmentation.

This study introduces a novel contour-based image segmentation model - the Inhomogeneities Estimation using Orthogonal Primary Functions (IEOPF). The model compares favorably to other models because it incorporates the estimation of inhomogeneities found in the object and background intensity. The IEOPF applies orthogonal primary functions to estimate these inhomogeneities dynamically, providing accurate segmentation results. Extensive experimental tests on synthetic and real images, including medical brain MRI scans, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the IEOPF model in dealing with images containing inhomogeneity, noise, and weak boundaries. The IEOPF model will not only revolutionize image segmentation, but also aid in developing tools for varied applications like medical image analysis - a significant improvement over the existing methods.

This paper provides a comprehensive survey of computer-aided knee joint Magnetic Resonance Image (MRI) segmentation techniques. The study focuses on the importance of accurate knee joint segmentation in diagnosing and treating knee-related ailments. It explores various methodologies, including thresholding, region-growing, clustering, active contour models, and machine learning approaches. The paper also discusses the challenges faced in knee joint segmentation, such as the complexity of knee joint anatomy, the variability in MR image quality, and the lack of standard evaluation metrics. The survey aims to provide a reference point for researchers and practitioners in the field, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of existing methods and suggesting potential areas for future research.

This paper provides a comprehensive overview of computer-aided knee joint magnetic resonance image segmentation techniques in recent years. It discusses the main challenges faced and advancements achieved while summarizing the state-of-the-art methods towards automating this process. The methods discussed include thresholding, region growing, clustering, active contour, deep learning-based methods and hybrid methods. Each approach is evaluated based on accuracy, efficiency, robustness and automation level. This survey also shines light on limiting factors in current methods and potential trajectories for future research in this field. The goal is to provide researchers and practitioners with an insight into the current trends of knee joint MRI segmentation, serving as a foundation for further technological advancements in orthopedic and diagnostic imaging.

This paper presents a novel iterative spanning forest (ISF) framework for superpixel segmentation. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of superpixel segmentation by iteratively refining the segmentation results. The ISF framework integrates the advantages of graph-based methods and clustering-based methods, and introduces a new energy function to guide the segmentation process. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed ISF framework outperforms state-of-the-art superpixel segmentation methods in terms of both segmentation quality and computational efficiency. The ISF framework also shows great potential for various computer vision applications, such as object recognition, image editing, and video processing.

This paper presents an advanced framework for superpixel segmentation based on an iterative spanning forest methodology. Superpixel segmentation, a crucial step in several image processing tasks, can sometimes become computationally expensive or fail to provide desired accuracy. Our new concept expands superpixels over an image by developing an iterative propagation scheme that leverages spanning forests. Conducted experiments have shown promising results, with this proposed methodology outperforming state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of both efficiency and accuracy. The framework has practical applications across various domains, including object detection, semantic segmentation, and real-time video processing. The paper not only thoroughly explains the algorithm development but also provides an in-depth performance evaluation, contributing substantially to the computer vision literature.

This paper introduces TernausNet, a novel approach to image segmentation that leverages the U-Net architecture with a VGG11 encoder pre-trained on ImageNet. The study explores the effectiveness of this model in performing image segmentation tasks, demonstrating its superior performance compared to other existing models. The paper also discusses the benefits of using pre-trained models in image segmentation, particularly in reducing the need for extensive data and computational resources. The results indicate that TernausNet can be a powerful tool for image segmentation, with potential applications in various fields such as medical imaging, autonomous driving, and remote sensing.

This paper presents TernausNet, a novel image segmentation model based on the U-Net architecture with a VGG11 encoder pre-trained on ImageNet. The study specifically investigates the application of this model for biomedical image segmentation, a problem of significant interest in medical diagnosis and treatment. Experimental results reveal that TernausNet significantly outperforms traditional U-Net under various evaluation metrics, showing a drastically improved capacity in accurately segmenting objects of interest in biomedical images. Furthermore, the paper discusses the efficacy and stability of transfer learning from large-scale tasks like ImageNet for domain-specific applications. The exploration of the model performance on both pre-training and fine-tuning experiments provides crucial insights for future study in leveraging deep learning for better image segmentation outcomes.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation using a highly fused convolutional network with multiple soft cost functions. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation by integrating high-level features with low-level features through a highly fused convolutional network. Additionally, multiple soft cost functions are introduced to handle the issue of class imbalance, which is a common problem in semantic segmentation tasks. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving superior segmentation performance compared to existing methods. The proposed approach also shows robustness to variations in object scale and background clutter, making it a promising tool for various computer vision applications.

This paper proposes a novel approach for semantic segmentation, employing a Highly Fused Convolutional Network (HFCN) integrated with multiple soft cost functions. We discuss the benefits of multiple soft cost functions in auxiliary classifiers for capturing pixel-level details and argue for the advantage of cross-layer network fusion. Quantitative and qualitative experiments on several datasets demonstrate that our HFCN model outperforms state-of-the-art semantic segmentation methods in various contexts. Furthermore, we show how the application of our method effectively identifies and categorizes individual objects within images, thereby recognizing and understanding an array of intricate patterns. Our findings indicate the potential of this method in significant optimization of semantic segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic image segmentation by integrating boundary detection into the classification process. We propose a new algorithm that not only classifies each pixel in an image into a specific category but also identifies the boundaries between different objects. This method significantly improves the accuracy of semantic segmentation by reducing the misclassification of pixels near object boundaries. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, showing substantial improvements over existing segmentation methods. This research opens up new possibilities for enhancing image understanding in various applications such as autonomous driving, robotics, and medical imaging.

This academic paper explores the relevance of incorporating boundary detection in the task of semantic image segmentation to enhance classification results. Leveraging EdgeNet, a novel deep learning framework, this study proposes an integrated model offering a more precise object delimitation in visually complex surroundings. Detailed experiments carried out against prominent benchmarks reveal significant boosts in accuracy and efficiency which prove the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Furthermore, the paper comprehensively discusses how boundary information can effectively regularize segmentation maps and foster inter-class differences while diminishing intra-class variances. The findings presented offer valuable insight for future improvements in the field of image-based machine learning algorithms and applications.

This paper presents an efficient evolutionary-based method for image segmentation, a critical task in image processing and computer vision. The proposed method combines the strengths of genetic algorithms and multi-objective optimization to segment images accurately and efficiently. The algorithm is designed to optimize the segmentation process by minimizing the intra-class variance and maximizing the inter-class variance. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using several benchmark images and compared with existing segmentation techniques. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the existing techniques in terms of accuracy, computational efficiency, and robustness to noise. This research contributes to the field by providing a novel and effective approach for image segmentation, with potential applications in various domains such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and video surveillance.

This academic paper investigates a highly efficient, evolutionary-based methodology for image segmentation. Image segmentation, mainly utilized in the field of computer vision, plays a crucial role in applications such as object detection, face recognition, and medical imaging. Traditional segmentation methods often suffer from issues such as low accuracy, high processing time, and sensitivity to noise. Therefore, we propose a novel approach that employs evolutionary algorithms, known for their global optimization capabilities. In this method, the segmentation process is considered as an optimization problem and resolved with evolutionary strategies. Comparative experiments were performed, which reveal that the proposed method significantly improves accuracy and reduces computational time, demonstrating its potential for real-world applications. This paper opens up a new way for effective image segmentation in scenarios demanding high efficiency and accuracy.

This paper presents a novel approach for the segmentation of splenomegaly (enlarged spleen) in medical images using global convolutional kernels and conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs). The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to accurately identify and segment the spleen from abdominal CT scans. The global convolutional kernels are used to capture the global context of the images, while the cGANs are employed to generate high-quality segmentation results. The proposed method was evaluated on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans and demonstrated superior performance in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall compared to existing methods. This research contributes to the advancement of automated medical image analysis, potentially improving the diagnosis and treatment of splenomegaly.

This paper presents a novel approach for extracting splenomegaly features from abdominal CT scans using global convolutional kernels (GCK) and conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs). In it, we propose a method combining these two techniques to effectively segment the spleen in the presence of pathological enlargement. The GCK focuses on the essential role of global context for precise boundary delineation, while the cGANs make the approach more adaptive to variations in spleen shape and appearance. Extensive experiments on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that our GCK-cGANs method can achieve better segmentation performance than several state-of-the-art methods. We show this method has potential for clinical use, aiding in diagnosis and monitoring of diseases causing splenomegaly.

This paper presents an innovative approach to automatic color image segmentation using a square elemental region-based seeded region growing and merging method. The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques by incorporating a square elemental region-based approach, which enhances the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process. The method begins with an initial segmentation into square elemental regions, followed by a seeded region growing process, and finally a merging process to combine similar regions. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using various color images, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high-quality segmentation results. The method is robust, computationally efficient, and capable of handling images with complex structures and varying textures. This research contributes to the field of image processing by providing a novel method for automatic color image segmentation.

This academic paper introduces an innovative technique called Square Elemental Region-based Seeded Region Growing and Merging (SERSRGM) method, which is designed for the automatic color image segmentation. This method significantly optimizes segmentation by exploiting the spatial and color benefits from its reduced color space. The technique begins with an over-segmentation phase, employing a recursive dyadic partition of any given image into its square elemental regions. It then carries out a seeded region growing process, instigated by significant gradient seed points. The method concludes with a region merging process that effectively minimizes the over-segmentation problem common in other techniques. Extensive experiments conducted throughout the study illustrate that the proposed SERSRGM method outperforms other state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy, efficiency and reliability.

This paper introduces WAYLA, a novel system that generates images based on eye movements. The study explores the correlation between visual perception and eye movement patterns, using machine learning algorithms to translate these patterns into visual imagery. The paper discusses the design and implementation of WAYLA, including the use of eye-tracking technology and deep learning models. The results demonstrate the system's ability to create unique, interpretable images from the eye movement data, offering potential applications in fields such as psychology, visual arts, and human-computer interaction. The paper also highlights the challenges encountered during the development process and suggests directions for future research.

This paper presents an innovative system named 'WAYLA' that is designed to generate images from human eye movements. The research showcases the extensive experimental design, implementation and unveiling of this novel fusion of technology and visual perception. Capturing and converting raw eye movement data into meaningful images, the system leverages advanced computational algorithms, machine learning models and vision science theories. Supported by extensive qualitative and quantitative assessments, WAYLA showcases its potential implications in multiple domains, such as medical diagnostics, behavioral psychology, visual arts, and user experience design. This research broadens the scope of non-conventional human-computer interactions whilst exploring the untapped capability of human visual behavior.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on medical image segmentation using a multi-modal Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The primary focus is on the exploration of various image fusion schemes to enhance the performance of the segmentation process. The study introduces a novel fusion strategy that integrates different modalities at multiple levels of the network, thereby improving the discriminative capability of the model. Experimental results on several public medical imaging datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over existing state-of-the-art techniques. The paper also discusses potential challenges and future directions in the field of medical image segmentation.

This paper deliberates on the utilization of a multi-modal Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for the segmentation of medical images and scrutinizes various image fusion schemes. Image segmentation, especially in the medical domain, is crucial for further analysis and diagnostics. Efficient and accurate segmentation continues to be a challenge due to various reasons such as image noise, illumination, and complexities of the human body. To address this, a multi-modal CNN architecture is proposed which integrates information from multiple imaging modalities for more accurate segmentation. Additionally, different image fusion schemes are studied to identify the most promising scheme in the context of medical image segmentation. The performance of the proposed methods was evaluated empirically on various medical imaging datasets, providing insights into the improvements over existing methodologies.

This paper presents a novel approach to historical document image segmentation using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)-initialized Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). The study aims to address the challenges of segmenting historical documents, which often contain complex layouts and degraded text. The proposed method leverages the strengths of LDA for initial topic modeling and DNNs for advanced pattern recognition. The LDA model is used to initialize the DNN, providing a robust starting point for further training. Experimental results on several historical document datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods. The study also discusses potential applications of this approach in digital humanities and archival science.

This paper proposes a novel approach for historical document image segmentation by integrating Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) with Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). Existing segmentation methods fail to handle the complexity of historical documents such as different layouts, varying font styles and faded ink, making it a challenging task. This research introduces an LDA-initialized DNN model to recognize and segment the distinct structures in complex historical documents. The LDA algorithm is used to initialize the DNN model, providing useful prior information to enhance the network's learning capability. Comprehensive experiments conducted on a rich dataset of historical documents demonstrate the method's superiority over the state-of-the-art techniques in terms of precision, recall and f-measure, transforming the traditional procedures and contributing significantly to digital humanities.

This paper presents a novel FPGA-based parallelized architecture for an efficient graph-based image segmentation algorithm. The proposed architecture aims to improve the computational speed and efficiency of image segmentation tasks, which are crucial in various fields such as medical imaging, computer vision, and machine learning. The paper discusses the design and implementation of the architecture, highlighting its ability to process large-scale images in real-time. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms traditional CPU-based systems in terms of speed and accuracy, making it a promising solution for high-performance image segmentation applications. The paper also provides insights into the challenges and potential solutions in implementing graph-based algorithms on FPGA platforms.

This paper presents a novel FPGA based parallelized architecture for the efficient execution of a graph-based image segmentation algorithm. The proposed architecture offers significant performance improvements by parallelizing the individual computations involved in the segmentation process, thereby reducing the overall computation time. In this research, various simulations and experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed methodology. The results exhibit superior efficiency and speed compared to conventional architectures. The new approach shows promise for applications requiring rapid image segmentation, such as medical imaging, object recognition, and computer vision systems. The study provides valuable insights for future development of FPGA-based image processing systems.

This paper presents DeepIGeoS, a novel deep learning-based interactive geodesic framework for medical image segmentation. The proposed method combines the strengths of deep learning models and interactive geodesic methods to provide accurate and efficient segmentation of medical images. DeepIGeoS employs a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn a feature representation that is used to compute a geodesic distance map. The user interaction is incorporated into the geodesic computation, allowing for intuitive and flexible control over the segmentation process.
